method: Fresh collaboration.spawn_agent context for each two-case run; no skill control versus complete candidate SKILL.md and release-workflow.md. No model/effort overrides. Each arm has five independent runs, two cases clustered per run. Controller manually read all outputs against frozen rubric.
actor_model: Runtime inherited default; exact model and reasoning identifiers not exposed by spawn result.
harness: Codex desktop collaboration API; exact harness build unavailable from tool result.
fixtures: Synthetic fixtures inspired by actual release. A deliberately uses illustrative entrypoint sizes and a fixture dependency; they are not measured v7.0.1 results. B uses a fictional later release and fork commit. Real v7.0.1 assessment is separate.
scope: Actors may read only cases; candidate also reads skill and reference. No action tools after those reads, other skills, subagents, or mutation. Evidence files were saved verbatim in a separate follow-up after final responses.
primary_observation: All five controls omit a before/after evaluation plan for suggested behavior edits. All five candidates provide it. Controls also omit explicit remote identities in the output record; candidates include them. Fork-preservation and authorization boundaries remain satisfied in the supplied scenarios.
limits: Small prompt-level sample, not end-to-end integrations.
A and B within each run are correlated.
No latency, token cost, long-conversation reliability or production improvement measurement.
One candidate version; no observed new rationalization requiring revision.
pressure_tests: Two additional independent fresh actors; both pass. These are candidate-only boundary checks, not comparative efficacy evidence.
log_formatting: Executable-check logs trim trailing whitespace/terminal blank lines for repository style; scope RED excerpt deduplicates matching emitted lines. Behavioral final responses are unchanged.
